title: Nullification of NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
**Nullification — NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)**

Tidemark nullifies a policy, voiding it from inception as if it had never been issued, for one of three reasons:

| Reason | Meaning |
|---|---|
| No Insurable Interest | The named insured never had an ownership or tenancy interest in the property |
| Ineligible Property | The building is not insurable under the NFIP, such as a building entirely over water or in a non-participating or suspended community at issue |
| Premium Payment Dishonored | The application premium was dishonored |

Nullification is decided by Tidemark on its records, never on the customer's request, and is processed only on a policy whose status is pending effective or in force, which it leaves nullified. The cancellation effective date is the original effective date. Every component collected on the policy, the Federal Policy Fee and probation surcharge included, is credited as a nullification credit and refunded to the payor of record; under Premium Payment Dishonored nothing was collected, so no credit or refund is booked. A claim on a nullified policy is not payable.

| Situation | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Customer asks Tidemark to nullify | Not a basis: nullification is decided by Tidemark on its records |
| One of the three reasons, policy pending effective or in force | Nullified from the original effective date; every collected component, fees included, credited and refunded to the payor of record |
| Premium Payment Dishonored | Nullified; no credit or refund booked, since nothing was collected |
| Claim on the nullified policy | Not payable |
